# Backup and Restore Lab

Run PowerShell commands from the repository root. If authorization is enabled, authenticate securely; avoid putting passwords in shell history. For this local lab, use the prompt-based `--password` option.

## A. Back up ShopDB

Create a backup folder outside the repository:

```
$stamp = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd-HHmmss"
$backupRoot = Join-Path $HOME "mongodb-dba-lab\backups"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $backupRoot | Out-Null
$dumpPath = Join-Path $backupRoot "ShopDB-$stamp"
mongodump --uri "mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017" --db ShopDB --out $dumpPath
Get-ChildItem $dumpPath -Recurse
```

If authentication is enabled, use `mongodump --uri "mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017" --username labAdmin --authenticationDatabase admin --password 12345 --db ShopDB --out $dumpPath` and enter the password at the prompt. Use an appropriately scoped backup account in a more realistic lab.

Expected: a `ShopDB` folder containing BSON data files and metadata. A successful command should report that collections were dumped.  
Output:  
![][image1]

## B. Restore into a separate database

Use the exact dump folder created above:

```
mongorestore --uri "mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017" --nsFrom="ShopDB.*" --nsTo="ShopDB_RestoreTest.*" "$dumpPath\ShopDB"
```

If authentication is enabled, add `--username labAdmin --authenticationDatabase admin --password` and enter the password when prompted. If your restore reports duplicate-key errors, you may have run it previously; for a clean test, drop only the lab target database first or use `--drop` carefully against the dedicated restore target.

## C. Validate restored data

```
 mongosh "mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017/ShopDB_RestoreTest" --username labAdmin --authenticationDatabase admin --password 12345 --eval "printjson({customers:db.customers.countDocuments(), products:db.products.countDocuments(), orders:db.orders.countDocuments()})"
```

Expected counts: customers 16, products 10, orders 12\. Validate a sample order:

```
 mongosh "mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017/ShopDB" --username labAdmin --authenticationDatabase admin --password 12345 --eval "printjson({customers:db.customers.countDocuments(), products:db.products.countDocuments(), orders:db.orders.countDocuments()})"
```

Document:

- Backup timestamp and path (do not commit the dump itself).  
- Command exit code / success output.  
- Collection counts before and after.  
- Any issue encountered and how it was resolved.  
- Recovery objective: for this small lab, state that the exercise validates logical backup/restore; do not claim production RPO/RTO without measured tests.

## D. Clean up

Only after evidence is captured, remove the test restore database if desired:

```
mongosh "mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017/ShopDB_RestoreTest" --username labAdmin --authenticationDatabase admin --password 12345 --eval "db.dropDatabase()"
```

Never run cleanup commands against a production database.
